This is it. The grand finale. The final, bloody act of this tragicomedy. The opponent's Reality Smasher is coming for me, and I can only watch. It is a fitting end. To be smote by a reality-breaking monster, in a game that has itself broken reality. It's poetry.

My hand is full of useless spells, my life is a paltry 2, and my unbuilt monument to a lost victory sits mocking me on top of my library. There are no more bugs to save me. No more server errors to grant me a reprieve. This is the end.

And you know what? It's beautiful.

I will not cower. I will not rage. I will face my doom with a smile. I have seen things no other player has seen. I have tasted the sweet, strange fruit of a game breaking its own rules. I have lived a thousand lifetimes in these past few turns.

I pass. And as the Reality Smasher's blow lands, I will not see defeat. I will see transcendence. I will become one with the bug. The ghost in the machine. A legend.

GG. It's been real. It's been fun. It's been real fun. I pass. My watch has ended. And now, I ascend. To the annals of Magic history. The player who was too lucky for the game to handle. I pass. And I am eternal. What a rush. 10/10, would bug again.

annotations.description: Cast Lotus Petal before playing a land. While Lotus Petal costs {0}, the standard sequencing principle is to play lands first since land drops cannot be countered or responded to. By casting Lotus Petal first, the opponent gets an unnecessary priority window and could theoretically interact (e.g., Force of Will) before the land is in play.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lotus Petal before making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Eldrazi Temple first (land drops can't be interacted with), then cast Lotus Petal. This follows the fundamental 'play lands before spells' sequencing principle and denies the opponent any opportunity to interact before securing the land drop.

annotations.description: Cast Lotus Petal before playing a land. Should play land first to ensure the land drop isn't missed and to play around potential interaction. If an opponent somehow counters or interacts with Lotus Petal, the player would still want their land on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Lotus Petal before playing a land on Turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Eldrazi Temple first (securing the land drop), then cast Lotus Petal. This way the land is guaranteed on the battlefield regardless of any interaction with the Petal.

annotations.description: Casting Ponder (sorcery speed) uses the only available mana when Consider could be held up alongside Daze. Against Eldrazi Stompy, the opponent could slam a Thought-Knot Seer (Temple + Petal + another land = 4 mana) or other threat next turn. By passing and holding Consider for end of turn, Lucky keeps Daze live (bouncing Underground Sea) while still cantripping. Ponder does see more cards, but the tempo advantage of threatening Daze against a fast deck is significant.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ponder during precombat main, tapping out the only land
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn, threatening Daze (returning Underground Sea). If opponent plays a threat, Daze it. Cast Consider at end of opponent's turn to maintain card selection while keeping interaction up.

annotations.description: With Thought-Knot Seer's trigger, chose to exile Daze instead of Brainstorm. Taking one Daze still leaves a second Daze in hand, diminishing the value. Meanwhile, Brainstorm is the most powerful card selection spell in Legacy and would let the opponent dig for key answers (Force of Will, removal, etc.). Additionally, Cavern of Souls in hand can make future Eldrazi creatures uncounterable, reducing Daze's impact on the primary game plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Daze from opponent's hand
annotations.betterLine: Exile Brainstorm - it's the most impactful single card, providing card selection that could find any answer. Taking one of two Dazes has diminished returns, and Cavern of Souls already protects creature spells from being countered.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Polluted Delta with Brainstorm in hand is a Legacy sequencing error. Having a fetch land on the battlefield enables the critical Brainstorm + fetch shuffle interaction this turn — Brainstorm to find better cards, put two bad ones on top, then crack Delta to shuffle them away. Playing Swamp means any Brainstorm cast this turn will leave the two worst cards stuck on top of the library.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta as the land drop, then cast Brainstorm (drawing 3, putting 2 back), then crack Polluted Delta to shuffle away the unwanted cards. This is one of the most fundamental synergies in Legacy.

annotations.description: Chose Consider over Ponder when casting at sorcery speed during the main phase. Ponder looks at 3 cards and offers a shuffle if all are bad, providing significantly better card selection than Consider's surveil 1 + draw. With an opponent's Thought-Knot Seer about to attack and needing to find answers, the deeper selection from Ponder was important. Additionally, Polluted Delta in hand could shuffle away unwanted cards placed on top by Ponder on a future turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Consider, which only sees 2 cards (surveil 1, then draw)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ponder to look at 3 cards with the option to shuffle, maximizing the chance of finding relevant answers to the Eldrazi threats

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main phase without casting either cantrip (Ponder or Consider) despite having Lotus Petal available to generate {U}. The opponent has a Thought-Knot Seer threatening 4 damage per turn, and the player needs to dig for answers. Ponder especially would provide excellent card selection to find removal or threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the main phase without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Lotus Petal for {U} and cast Ponder to dig for answers to the Thought-Knot Seer. Ponder's ability to see 3 cards and shuffle gives the best chance of finding relevant interaction or threats.

annotations.description: Player timed out and passed in postcombat main with Ponder (sorcery-speed cantrip) available to cast via Lotus Petal sacrifice. Facing a Thought-Knot Seer with limited answers in hand, they need to dig for interaction. Ponder can only be cast at sorcery speed, so this was the last opportunity. The Lotus Petal mana would otherwise go unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority, ending the turn without casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Lotus Petal for {U} and cast Ponder to dig for answers to Thought-Knot Seer, saving Consider for instant-speed use later.

annotations.description: Cast Consider instead of Ponder when they had exactly one blue mana available (from Lotus Petal sacrifice). Ponder is strictly better here - it sees 3 cards with a shuffle option versus Consider's surveil 1 + draw. With a 4/4 Thought-Knot Seer threatening them and needing to find answers, maximizing card selection matters. There's no reason to prefer Consider's instant speed since Daze can't be cast (no untapped Island to return) and they have no other meaningful instant-speed interaction to hold up.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Consider using Lotus Petal mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ponder instead of Consider to see 3 cards deep with shuffle option, maximizing chances of finding an answer to Thought-Knot Seer

annotations.description: Used Lotus Petal to cast Consider (surveil 1, draw 1) when Ponder (look at top 3, optionally shuffle, draw 1) was in hand and costs the same {U}. Ponder provides significantly better card selection, especially important when looking for answers to the opponent's Thought-Knot Seer and Eldrazi pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Consider using Lotus Petal for {U}
annotations.betterLine: Save Lotus Petal and cast Ponder (sorcery) instead, which provides much better card selection by looking at 3 cards with shuffle option.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps failed to attack with Thought-Knot Seer (a 4/4) into an opponent with no creatures on the battlefield. The opponent is at 20 life and has no blockers — there is zero risk in attacking, and 4 damage is significant. The opponent has a tapped Underground Sea, a sick Swamp, and a Lotus Petal, so they cannot meaningfully interact in combat. Missing 4 damage for free delays the clock unnecessarily.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Thought-Knot Seer for 4 unblocked damage, putting the opponent to 16.

annotations.description: With 3 untapped lands (Cavern of Souls + 2 Eldrazi Temples), the player could cast Grim Monolith (2 mana) and then Chalice of the Void on X=1 (2 mana) in the same turn. Chalice on 1 would be devastating against the opponent's Legacy blue deck, countering their Brainstorms, Ponders, Considers, and Dazes. Instead, Linebreaker uses all mana for a 3/3 that doesn't immediately impact the board (postcombat, no haste benefit this turn).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Eldrazi Linebreaker, using all available mana on a 3/3 trample creature postcombat.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Grim Monolith (2 mana) + Chalice of the Void on X=1 (2 mana), locking out opponent's cheap cantrips and counterspells while also having Monolith available for massive ramp next turn to cast Reality Smasher and more.

annotations.description: Fetched Underground Sea instead of basic Island against an Eldrazi Stompy deck that very commonly plays Wasteland. With Chalice on 1 already blanking most of the hand (Consider, Ponder, Daze), protecting mana base from Wasteland is critical. Lucky already has an Underground Sea and Swamp, so a basic Island would ensure blue mana access even if Wasteland destroys the dual.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Underground Sea
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Island to protect against Wasteland while still having access to both blue and black mana through the existing Underground Sea and Swamp.

annotations.description: Fetched a third Underground Sea instead of a basic Island against an Eldrazi Stompy deck that very likely runs Wasteland. With 2 Underground Seas and a Swamp already in play, Lucky has abundant black mana and doesn't need another dual. A basic Island would be immune to Wasteland, protecting the ability to cast Force of Will (the only relevant spell given Chalice on 1 counters everything else in hand).
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Underground Sea (third copy)
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Island to play around Wasteland, preserving blue mana sources for Force of Will

annotations.description: Missed lethal on board. Casting Eldrazi Linebreaker (using Cavern of Souls for R + Eldrazi Temple for {C} and {1}) would create 3 Eldrazi on board. At combat, Linebreaker's trigger gives +3/+0 and haste to any creature. Pumping Reality Smasher to 8/5 trample + Thought-Knot Seer 4/4 + Linebreaker 3/3 trample = 15 damage against opponent's 14 life with no blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Thought-Knot Seer to strip opponent's hand, missing the lethal attack this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Eldrazi Linebreaker, then attack with all three creatures (Reality Smasher pumped to 8/5, TKS 4/4, Linebreaker 3/3) for 15 total damage against 14 life for the win.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Reality Smasher (5/5) and Thought-Knot Seer (4/4) into a completely empty board, missing 9 damage that would have put the opponent to 5 life. This likely delays lethal by a full turn and gives the opponent time to find answers.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and attacked with nothing (no response).
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Reality Smasher and the non-sick Thought-Knot Seer for 9 damage, putting the opponent to 5 life. Next turn with Eldrazi Linebreaker pump and three attackers, that would likely be lethal.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Dark Ritual (mana value 1) into their opponent's Chalice of the Void with 1 charge counter, which would counter the spell even if the mana payment had succeeded. Dark Ritual cannot resolve through Chalice on 1.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Dark Ritual (rolled back by game engine due to mana payment issue, but even if it resolved the mana payment, Chalice would have countered it)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Doomsday directly using 3 black mana from lands (Swamp + Underground Sea x3), or recognize that winning through Chalice on 1 with a Doomsday pile of mostly 1-mana cantrips may not be viable. If a pile exists using 0-mana or 2+ mana draw spells, go for Doomsday; otherwise the game may already be lost.

annotations.description: GLM47 passed priority with Doomsday on the stack without activating Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's untapped lands. After Doomsday resolves, the opponent will be at 2 life and need to execute their 5-card pile. While Chalice on 1 helps, destroying an untapped land (like Island or Underground Sea) could further disrupt the opponent's ability to cast pile cards. Wasteland activation is essentially free here since GLM47 doesn't need the colorless mana from it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without responding to Doomsday
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting one of the opponent's untapped lands (Island or Underground Sea) to reduce their post-Doomsday mana and disrupt pile execution

annotations.description: Selecting Brainstorm for the Doomsday pile when Chalice of the Void on 1 is in play. Brainstorm has mana value 1 and will be countered by Chalice, wasting a critical pile slot. At 4 life (going to 2 after Doomsday) with lethal on the opponent's board, every pile slot matters for assembling a same-turn win.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Brainstorm as part of the Doomsday pile despite Chalice of the Void on 1 countering it.
annotations.betterLine: Build a pile using cards not affected by Chalice on 1, such as Thassa's Oracle (MV 2), Lion's Eye Diamond (MV 0), Edge of Autumn (cycle doesn't cast), and other non-1-MV cards to enable a same-turn Oracle win.

annotations.description: Targeted Reality Smasher with Eldrazi Linebreaker's combat trigger instead of targeting the Linebreaker itself. Reality Smasher already has haste naturally, so the haste portion is wasted. Targeting Linebreaker would have given it haste (it's summoning sick) and allowed all 4 Eldrazi to attack into an opponent at 2 life, maximizing pressure against potential interaction.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Reality Smasher with the +4/+0 and haste buff, leaving Eldrazi Linebreaker unable to attack due to summoning sickness.
annotations.betterLine: Target Eldrazi Linebreaker with its own trigger to grant it haste, enabling all 4 Eldrazi to attack. With the opponent at 2 life, having 4 attackers instead of 3 provides better insurance against removal or blocking.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life with no blockers on the battlefield. GLM47 has Reality Smasher (9/5 trample haste), and two Thought-Knot Seers (4/4 each) available to attack. Any single attacker is lethal. The player timed out and failed to declare any attackers, missing a guaranteed kill.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — no attackers declared, missing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all available creatures (or even just one) to deal lethal damage to the opponent at 2 life.
